findings.title: White House nominates Palantir's LoSapio to lead Homeland Security's cyber agency
findings.summary_md: The White House said on Monday it nominated Michael LoSapio to be director of the Department of Homeland Security's Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. LoSapio will take over from acting director Nick Andersen, and the agency has been without a Senate-confirmed leader for almost 22 months. CISA's staffing has fallen by about a third since Trump took power in 2025, and the nomination follows three large-scale breaches at DHS, the FBI and the Pentagon disclosed in the past three months. LoSapio, Palantir's chief information security officer, did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

findings.title: Trump nominates Palantir security chief Michael LoSapio to lead CISA
findings.summary_md: President Donald Trump nominated Palantir chief information security officer Michael LoSapio to lead CISA on Monday, seeking to fill a leadership vacancy that has stretched through nearly two years of staffing cuts. LoSapio would oversee the federal government's main civilian cyberdefense unit, which helps protect agency networks and works with operators of water, power, telecom and other critical infrastructure. CISA has been without a permanent Senate-confirmed director since Jen Easterly's departure in January 2025, with Nick Andersen leading the agency in an acting capacity since February. LoSapio has served as Palantir's CISO since September 2024, after leading the company's infrastructure and network security group from December 2017.

findings.title: Trump picks Palantir's LoSapio to head CISA
findings.summary_md: President Donald Trump on Monday nominated Michael LoSapio, chief information security officer at Palantir, to lead CISA, which has been without a Senate-confirmed director for the entirety of Trump's second term. CISA's first pick, Sean Plankey, languished in the Senate before withdrawing in April. LoSapio could face obstacles because Palantir is unpopular with Democrats, who have scrutinized the company's work with the Department of Homeland Security even as Palantir denies aiding mass surveillance of immigrants. Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., had placed one of several Senate holds on Plankey pending release of a public telecom cybersecurity report, and some observers expected acting director Nick Andersen to continue holding the role.

findings.title: Trump picks Palantir cybersecurity executive to lead CISA
findings.summary_md: President Donald Trump nominated Michael LoSapio, CISO of Palantir, to lead CISA on Monday; the agency has been without a Senate-confirmed director since the end of the Biden administration and Trump's first nominee withdrew in April. LoSapio has no significant management background and appears never to have worked in government, spending two decades as an engineer including stints at three universities and a year as a site reliability engineer at SingleStore. He was a system engineer at Palantir in the mid-2010s, left, and rejoined in 2017, serving as head of network security from 2017 to 2024 and CISO since September 2024. If confirmed he would face rebuilding CISA's capacity after two years of layoffs, resignations, program freezes, service reductions and political attacks that eroded partner trust.

findings.title: Trump taps Palantir security chief to run battered US cyber defense agency
findings.summary_md: President Donald Trump nominated Palantir security chief Michael LoSapio to lead CISA, a move that could end the agency's nearly two-year wait for a Senate-confirmed director after Jen Easterly's January 2025 departure. CISA has shed more than 1,000 staff, roughly a third of its workforce, since Trump returned to the White House, and acting director Nick Andersen said in September that about 250 recruits were still waiting for security clearance. LoSapio is Trump's second nominee for the role; Sean Plankey withdrew in April after more than a year awaiting confirmation amid a dispute involving Senator Rick Scott over Coast Guard contracting. Palantir, co-founded by Peter Thiel, is a major supplier to DHS and ICE, and its immigration work has drawn criticism from civil liberties groups and Democratic lawmakers.

findings.title: Palantir exec nominated to lead CISA; lame-duck Senate vote is uncertain
findings.summary_md: President Donald Trump nominated Palantir chief information security officer Michael LoSapio to lead CISA on Monday, selecting him to head an agency that has been without a Senate-confirmed leader since Trump returned to the Oval Office. CISA lost more than 1,000 personnel, one-third of its workforce, and saw its budget slashed by billions during the second Trump administration, and it remained largely behind the scenes ahead of last week's midterm elections. Nick Andersen has led the agency in an acting capacity since February after Madhu Gottumukkala was reassigned, and Sean Plankey withdrew earlier this year after months in limbo. It is unclear whether the Senate will take up the nomination during the lame-duck session, and if lawmakers adjourn without approving it Trump would have to renominate LoSapio for an incoming Democratic majority.

findings.title: Palantir CISO Michael LoSapio Nominated to Lead CISA
findings.summary_md: The White House said Monday it sent Michael LoSapio's nomination to the Senate to serve as director of DHS's Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. CISA's top post has had no Senate-confirmed occupant since Jen Easterly stepped down in January 2025; Sean Plankey withdrew in April after more than a year awaiting confirmation, Madhu Gottumukkala led in an acting capacity until February, and Nick Andersen has served as acting director since then. LoSapio has served as Palantir's CISO since 2024, joined the company in 2013 as a systems engineer, and led its infrastructure and network security group from 2017 to 2024 after earlier work as a Linux systems engineer at three universities. The nomination comes as CISA works through a broad reshaping of its leadership and strategy while operating without a Senate-confirmed director.
